findings.title: Four detectors emit recommendation claims without structured provenance
findings.where: The recommendation objects returned at the cited lines contain calculated counts, rates, thresholds, or causal/inferential wording but no provenance property.
findings.what: Consumers cannot reproduce these recommendations from a cited artifact and parsed field or distinguish observations from inference. stale-projects reports count/age from projects; bloated-claude-md reports a merged line count and adherence conclusion; compaction-hot-sessions reports fleet risk and reclaim calculations; compaction-large-tool-outputs reports mean rate and dominant-session counts. All omit structured provenance.
findings.fix: Add non-empty provenance.observations entries citing each source artifact/parser and field with reproducible values, plus a separate inference string. Add each migrated detector ID to the provenance contract and assert validation in its behavioral test.
findings.acceptance: For a firing fixture of each detector, validateRecommendationProvenance returns an empty array; observations cite the exact input field/parser behind every displayed number, and mutation of that field reproducibly changes the cited value.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed each cited return object lacks provenance. The directly related baseline contract defines observations/source/field/value and inference; although its allowlist migration is incremental, this audit's active gate explicitly requires structured provenance for every recommendation claim.

findings.title: Hot-session threshold can label a single session as “Multiple sessions”
findings.where: The guard returns only when both hotSessions < 2 and hotPercent < 40, while the emitted title unconditionally says “Multiple sessions.”
findings.what: A corpus with one hot session comprising at least 40% of the fleet passes the guard and emits a factually false plural title. The existing test verifies only the two-session case and does not protect this boundary.
findings.fix: Either require MIN_HOT_SESSIONS independently before emitting the plural recommendation, or select singular/plural title and detail based on summary.hotSessions; add a one-hot-session fixture at or above 40%.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with one hot session and hotPercent >= 40 either returns null or emits singular wording; two hot sessions still emit the plural title.
findings.verifyNote: A separate re-read confirmed the boolean condition is an OR trigger (the negated guard uses &&) and the returned title is invariant, so hotSessions=1 and hotPercent>=40 reaches the plural recommendation.

findings.title: Trailing newline makes the CLAUDE.md line threshold off by one
findings.where: The detector uses text.split('\n').length, while the boundary test does not exercise exactly 200 newline-terminated lines.
findings.what: A conventional file containing exactly 200 lines and ending in a newline produces 201 split elements and is warned despite the documented <=200 silent boundary. Displayed affected/line counts are likewise one too high for newline-terminated content.
findings.fix: Count line breaks while excluding the terminal empty split element, or normalize one terminal newline before splitting; add exact 200- and 201-line cases with and without final newlines.
findings.acceptance: Both newline-terminated and unterminated 200-line inputs return null and both 201-line forms emit affected=201.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the split result includes a terminal empty element and the current test's purported boundary case uses only 150 lines, so no assertion covers the failing 200-line form.
